notes: Two new modes that deal in real numbers instead of proxies. Measure asks the engine what your objects actually cost: it reads SceneDrawcallCount and SceneTriangleCount, makes the selected objects stop rendering for a few frames, reads them again, and reports the difference. That is a true triangle count even on meshes you don't own - the ones the Triangles mode can only estimate, which on most places is nearly all of them - plus the first per-object draw call figure the plugin has ever given. Nothing is written to your place: only LocalTransparencyModifier is touched, it is not serialised, and it is always restored. Select objects and pick Measure, or pick it with nothing selected to confirm the worst offenders of your last scan. Draw calls is the whole-place counterpart: it groups every renderable by what the engine can batch together (mesh, texture, surface appearance, material, transparency and shadow pass) and reports roughly how many draw calls it takes to draw your place, which assets are used exactly once and pay a full draw call for a single object, and which are reused across thousands. The estimate is printed next to the engine's own count so you can see the error rather than take it on trust. Both are labelled honestly: Measure reports what the current camera sees at the margin, so an object off-screen or sharing a batch with others measures zero, and it says so instead of calling it free.
